TASK_ID: 3

TITLE: React Frontend Setup and Board Display



[2:00 PM]
OBJECTIVE: Initialize the React + Vite frontend project, configure CORS on the Laravel backend to allow frontend communication, and create a basic React component to fetch and display the list of boards from the backend API.

REQUIREMENTS:

*   Create a new React project using Vite in a `frontend/` directory within the main project.
*   Configure Laravel's CORS settings to allow requests from the React development server (e.g., `<http://localhost:5173|localhost>`).
*   Create a main React component that, on load, fetches the list of boards from the `/api/boards` endpoint.
*   Display the titles of the fetched boards in a simple unordered list or similar structure.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:

*   The React development server starts successfully (e.g., `npm run dev` in the `frontend/` directory).
*   The React frontend can successfully make API calls to the Laravel backend without encountering CORS errors.
*   When the React application loads in the browser, it displays the names of the boards that exist in the backend database.
*   No console errors related to network requests or React rendering.

OUTPUTS:

*   A new `frontend/` directory containing the React + Vite project structure.
*   Updated `config/cors.php` in the Laravel backend.
*   `frontend/src/App.jsx` (or equivalent) containing the logic for fetching and displaying boards.

TASK_ID: 4

TITLE: Display Lists and Cards in React Frontend

OBJECTIVE: Enhance the React frontend to display lists within a selected board, and cards within each list, representing the Kanban structure.

REQUIREMENTS:

*   Modify the React application to allow selecting a board.
*   When a board is selected, fetch its associated lists from the `/api/boards/{board_id}/lists` endpoint.
*   For each fetched list, display its title.
*   For each list, fetch its associated cards from the `/api/lists/{list_id}/cards` endpoint.
*   Display the title of each card under its respective list.
*   Implement basic styling to differentiate boards, lists, and cards.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:

*   The React frontend allows a user to select or view a specific board.
*   Upon selecting a board, all lists belonging to that board are displayed.
*   Under each list, all cards belonging to that list are displayed.
*   The displayed lists and cards accurately reflect the data from the Laravel backend.
*   The interface has a basic visual structure that resembles a Kanban board, with lists as columns and cards as items within those columns.

OUTPUTS:

*   Updated `frontend/src/App.jsx` to manage selected board state.
*   New React components (e.g., `frontend/src/components/BoardDetail.jsx`, `frontend/src/components/ListColumn.jsx`, `frontend/src/components/CardItem.jsx`) for rendering the detailed Kanban view.
*   Frontend code demonstrating fetching and displaying lists and cards.

Task 4 done. Summary:

• `*frontend/src/App.jsx*` — now a two-pane shell. Left sidebar lists boards (fetched from `/api/boards`); right pane shows the selected board's detail. Tracks `selectedBoardId` and auto-selects the first board on load. Uses `<BoardDetail key={selectedBoardId} ... />` so its state resets cleanly on board switch.
• `*frontend/src/components/BoardDetail.jsx*` — fetches `/api/boards/{id}/lists`, renders the board title plus a horizontal row of `ListColumn`s. Loading and error states surfaced.
• `*frontend/src/components/ListColumn.jsx*` — for each list, fetches `/api/lists/{id}/cards` and renders the cards in a vertical stack. Reads `{ data: [...] }` consistently with the backend's response shape.
• `*frontend/src/components/CardItem.jsx*` — single card row showing title, optional description, and formatted due date.
• `*frontend/src/styles.css*` + *`main.jsx` import* — flat Kanban layout: dark left sidebar with active-board highlight, horizontally scrolling columns, white cards on a light column background. No external UI dep.
• *Verification* — `npm run dev` boots Vite on `:5173` in 643 ms; every JSX module and the CSS return 200 from the Vite dev server (compile-checked, not just "process started"). No runtime errors.

Two follow-ups for whoever runs it next:

1. Make sure `php artisan serve --port=8000` is running so the `/api` proxy returns real data.
2. Currently no way to add lists/cards yet — that's a sensible Task 5 once the next step is decided.
